commentary: Eight activities this week against last week's seven — you're building momentum, and the pattern of pairing a morning swim with a weights session on the same day is starting to look less like a coincidence and more like a personality. The Saturday run went from 9.0km to 9.6km and the heart rate barely blinked, which is exactly the kind of quiet proof that the body is adapting whether you're paying attention or not. Last Friday's 901 metres at 98 bpm was clearly a "I showed up and that's enough" swim, which, fair, but four clean 2000 metre swims in a row this week suggests you came back from that with something to prove. The lifting cadence is still a little scrambled — chest and back appearing twice this week while legs only got one showing — but honestly, the consistency of just being in the room every single day is doing more work than the programming chaos can undo.
metrics_commentary: Eight kilometres in the pool and nearly ten on his feet — the body doing all of that in a single week is not a body that is messing around. HRV sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56 tells me the nervous system is recovering well and honestly looking a little smug about it, which is valid. VO2 Max at 53.1 is genuinely impressive, that is cardiovascular fitness that turns heads in the best possible way. The one thing I am clocking is that the run and walk came in across only one session, so the legs want more chances to show off — give them the opportunity, because they are clearly ready for it.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions this week, which means one slipped through the cracks, and we are absolutely noting that — but then again, the man walked in and added nearly seven kilograms to his overhead press in a single bound, going from 40.0 to 46.7 kg estimated one-rep max, and honestly that kind of thing earns a little grace. Weekly volume climbed from 20,753 to 22,867 kg, the seated leg curl crept up, the lat pulldown nudged forward, and the overall direction of this thing is unmistakably upward. Four sessions next week, babes — the shoulders clearly have more to say, and we are not leaving that conversation on the table.
